title: Dasakam 100 — Bhagavataḥ Keśādipādavarṇanam
description: Bhattathiri’s sequential meditation on Krishna’s youthful divine form, from the first vision through hair, eyes, face, flute, chest, waist and legs to the auspicious feet, ending with a prayer for forgiveness and well-being.
translation_note: No vetted English stanza translation is present in the supplied source bundle; translation_en is intentionally empty pending editorial review. Supplied photo captions remain verbatim commentary, not translation.

stanzas.sanskrit:
अग्रे पश्यामि तेजो निबिडतरकलायावलीलोभनीयं
पीयूषाप्लावितोऽहं तदनु तदुदरे दिव्यकैशोरवेषम् ।
तारुण्यारम्भरम्यं परमसुखरसास्वादरोमाञ्चिताङ्गै-
-रावीतं नारदाद्यैविलसदुपनिषत्सुन्दरीमण्डलैश्च ॥ १००-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhattathiri saw a bunch of blue lilly flowers spreading radiance and felt soaked in nectar. In the middle of the halo, Bhattathiri, in divine ecstasy, saw a beautiful young divine body form , surrounded by Narada and other sages and upanishads in the form of group of women.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
agre paśyāmi tejo nibiḍatarakalāyāvalīlobhanīyaṃ
pīyūṣāplāvito’haṃ tadanu tadudare divyakaiśoraveṣam |
tāruṇyārambharamyaṃ paramasukharasāsvādaromāñcitāṅgai-
-rāvītaṃ nāradādyaivilasadupaniṣatsundarīmaṇḍalaiśca || 100-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
नीलाभं कुञ्चिताग्रं घनममलतरं सम्यतं चारुभङ्ग्या
रत्नोत्तंसाभिरामं वलयितमुदयच्चन्द्रकैः पिञ्छजालैः ।
मन्दारस्रङ्निवीतं तव पृथुकबरीभारमालोकयेऽहं
स्निग्धश्वेतोर्ध्वपुण्ड्रामपि च सुललितां फालबालेन्दुवीथीम् ॥ १००-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhattathiri saw dark, curly, thick and very clean luxuriant locks of hair jewelled beautifully tied together with peacock feathers having glistening eyes, encircled by a garland of mandaaram flowers. He saw Bhagwan’s broad smooth forehead with soft, white, upright sandal paste mark, like a young moon's line.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
nīlābhaṃ kuñcitāgraṃ ghanamamalataraṃ samyataṃ cārubhaṅgyā
ratnottaṃsābhirāmaṃ valayitamudayaccandrakaiḥ piñchajālaiḥ |
mandārasraṅnivītaṃ tava pṛthukabarībhāramālokaye’haṃ
snigdhaśvetordhvapuṇḍrāmapi ca sulalitāṃ phālabālenduvīthīm || 100-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
हृद्यं पूर्णानुकम्पार्णवमृदुलहरीचञ्चलद्भ्रूविलासै-
-रानीलस्निग्धपक्ष्मावलिपरिलसितं नेत्रयुग्मं विभो ते ।
सान्द्रच्छायं विशालारुणकमलदलाकारमामुग्धतारं
कारुण्यालोकलीलाशिशिरितभुवनं क्षिप्यतां मय्यनाथे ॥ १००-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan’s eyebrows were attractive like the waves of the ocean filled with compassion. The eyes were lustrous with beautiful bluish eyelashes. They were shaped like big red lotus petals with beautiful pupils cooling the worlds.Bhattathiri requested Bhagwan to glance him with  compassion.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
hṛdyaṃ pūrṇānukampārṇavamṛdulaharīcañcaladbhrūvilāsai-
-rānīlasnigdhapakṣmāvaliparilasitaṃ netrayugmaṃ vibho te |
sāndracchāyaṃ viśālāruṇakamaladalākāramāmugdhatāraṃ
kāruṇyālokalīlāśiśiritabhuvanaṃ kṣipyatāṃ mayyanāthe || 100-3 ||

stanzas.commentary_en: The face of Bhagwan looked very beautiful with prominent, well shaped nose, cheeks shining like mirror made up of emerald stones, which seem to reflect the pair of fish shaped gem studded earrings, swinging from the ears. HIS ruby red lips similar to bimba fruit parts, revealed a beautiful shining row of white teeth and sported the captivating smile.

stanzas.sanskrit:
बाहुद्वन्द्वेन रत्नोज्ज्वलवलयभृता शोणपाणिप्रवाले-
-नोपात्तां वेणुनालीं प्रसृतनखमयूखाङ्गुलीसङ्गशाराम् ।
कृत्वा वक्त्रारविन्दे सुमधुरविकसद्रागमुद्भाव्यमानैः
शब्दब्रह्मामृतैस्त्वं शिशिरितभुवनैः सिञ्च मे कर्णवीथीम् ॥ १००-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan’s hands were covered by studded shining bangles, held the flute which was made colourful by the contact of HIS radiant finger nails. The flute kept in HIS lotus mouth gave out the blissful melodies & the music was Brahman itself flowing in the form of sound which can cool all the worlds. Bhattathiri prayed to Bhagwan to let his ears be drenched with such  divine music.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bāhudvandvena ratnojjvalavalayabhṛtā śoṇapāṇipravāle-
-nopāttāṃ veṇunālīṃ prasṛtanakhamayūkhāṅgulīsaṅgaśārām |
kṛtvā vaktrāravinde sumadhuravikasadrāgamudbhāvyamānaiḥ
śabdabrahmāmṛtaistvaṃ śiśiritabhuvanaiḥ siñca me karṇavīthīm || 100-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
उत्सर्पत् कौस्तुभश्रीततिभिररुणितं कोमलं कण्ठदेशं
वक्षः श्रीवत्सरम्यं तरलतरसमुद्दीप्रहारप्रतानम् ।
नानावर्णप्रसूनावलिकिसलयिनीं वन्यमालां विलोल-
-ल्लोलम्बां लम्बमानामुरसि तव तथा भावये रत्नमालाम् ॥ १००-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The shining Kaustubh jewel emitted radiance, making Bhagwan’s beautiful neck more reddish in colour. The chest was decked with array of shining pearl  & gem necklaces with Srivatsa mark. The garland of forest flowers full of nectar, with bees sitting on them, together with emerald necklaces further decorated HIS chest. Bhattathiri meditated on that beautiful chest of Bhagwan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
utsarpat kaustubhaśrītatibhiraruṇitaṃ komalaṃ kaṇṭhadeśaṃ
vakṣaḥ śrīvatsaramyaṃ taralatarasamuddīprahārapratānam |
nānāvarṇaprasūnāvalikisalayinīṃ vanyamālāṃ vilola-
-llolambāṃ lambamānāmurasi tava tathā bhāvaye ratnamālām || 100-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अङ्गे पञ्चाङ्गरागैरतिशयविकसत् सौरभाकृष्टलोकं
लीनानेकत्रिलोकीविततिमपि कृशां बिभ्रतं मध्यवल्लीम् ।
शक्राश्मन्यस्ततप्तोज्ज्वलकनकनिभं पीतचेलं दधानं
ध्यायामो दीप्तरश्मिस्फुटमणिरशनाकिङ्किणीमण्डितं त्वाम् ॥ १००-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Meditating on Bhagwan’s beautiful body which is smeared with the scent of five different types of flowers, one who holds the entire three worlds within, had a waist, slender like a creeper, whose body resembled a rock of sapphire which is covered with golden colour silk, which was held firmly to his hip with a shining gem studded girdle with hanging small bells.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
aṅge pañcāṅgarāgairatiśayavikasat saurabhākṛṣṭalokaṃ
līnānekatrilokīvitatimapi kṛśāṃ bibhrataṃ madhyavallīm |
śakrāśmanyastataptojjvalakanakanibhaṃ pītacelaṃ dadhānaṃ
dhyāyāmo dīptaraśmisphuṭamaṇiraśanākiṅkiṇīmaṇḍitaṃ tvām || 100-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ऊरू चारू तवोरू घनमसृणरुचौ चित्तचोरौ रमायाः
विश्वक्षोभं विशङ्क्य ध्रुवमनिशमुभौ पीतचेलावृताङ्गौ ।
आनम्राणां पुरस्तान्न्यसनधृतसमस्तार्थपालीसमुद्ग-
-च्छायं जानुद्वयं च क्रमपृथुलमनोज्ञे च जङ्घे निषेवे ॥ १००-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhattathiri meditated on Bhagwan’s two handsome thighs, solid, soft and charming, which stole Lakshmi's heart. The thighs were always covered with yellow silk cloth so as to prevent the world from getting excited at it. HIS two knees appeared like two caskets holding all the desired objects for his devotees, and HIS two ankles, beautifully tapered and fleshy.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ūrū cārū tavorū ghanamasṛṇarucau cittacorau ramāyāḥ
viśvakṣobhaṃ viśaṅkya dhruvamaniśamubhau pītacelāvṛtāṅgau |
ānamrāṇāṃ purastānnyasanadhṛtasamastārthapālīsamudga-
-cchāyaṃ jānudvayaṃ ca kramapṛthulamanojñe ca jaṅghe niṣeve || 100-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
मञ्जीरं मञ्जुनादैरिव पदभजनं श्रेय इत्यालपन्तं
पादाग्रं भ्रान्तिमज्जत् प्रणतजनमनोमन्दरोद्धारकूर्मम् ।
उत्तुङ्गाताम्रराजन्नखरहिमकरज्योत्स्नया चाऽऽश्रितानां
सन्तापध्वान्तहन्त्रीं ततिमनुकलये मङ्गलामङ्गुलीनाम् ॥ १००-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhattathiri meditated on Bhagwan’s anklets with their sweet sound, which, sweetly confirm the excellence of worshipping at HIS feet. Krishna’s incarnation of the tortoise which lifted up the Mandaar mountain, is lifting up the minds of the people who prostrate at Bhagwan’s feet. The slightly raised toe nails of Bhagwan’s auspicious toes are red and shining like the moon light expelling the darkness of the sorrows of devotees.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
mañjīraṃ mañjunādairiva padabhajanaṃ śreya ityālapantaṃ
pādāgraṃ bhrāntimajjat praṇatajanamanomandaroddhārakūrmam |
uttuṅgātāmrarājannakharahimakarajyotsnayā cā”śritānāṃ
santāpadhvāntahantrīṃ tatimanukalaye maṅgalāmaṅgulīnām || 100-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
योगीन्द्राणां त्वदङ्गेष्वधिकसुमधुरं मुक्तिभाजां निवासो
भक्तानां कामवर्षद्युतरुकिसलयं नाथ ते पादमूलम् ।
नित्यं चित्तस्थितं मे पवनपुरपते कृष्ण कारुण्यसिन्धो
हृत्वा निश्शेषतापान् प्रदिशतु परमानन्दसन्दोहलक्ष्मīm ॥ १००-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Among the parts of Bhagwan’s body, the soles of HIS feet are the most beloved and coveted to the great yogis. The liberated ones reside there. Bhattathiri prayed to Bhagwan, the Lord of Guruvayoor, the Ocean of compassion to rest those feet always in his heart and destroy all his sorrows and confer an abundant flow of supreme bliss.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
yogīndrāṇāṃ tvadaṅgeṣvadhikasumadhuraṃ muktibhājāṃ nivāso
bhaktānāṃ kāmavarṣadyutarukisalayaṃ nātha te pādamūlam |
nityaṃ cittasthitaṃ me pavanapurapate kṛṣṇa kāruṇyasindho
hṛtvā niśśeṣatāpān pradiśatu paramānandasandohalakṣmīm || 100-10 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अज्ञात्वा ते महत्त्वं यदिह निगदितं विश्वनाथ क्षमेथाः
स्तोत्रं चैतत् सहस्रोत्तरमधिकतरं त्वत्प्रसादाय भूयात् ।
द्वेधा नारायणीयं श्रुतिषु च जनुषा स्तुत्यतावर्णनेन
स्फीतं लीलावतारैरिदमिह कुरुतामायुरारोग्यसौख्यम् ॥ १००-११ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Bhattathiri sought forgiveness from Bhagwan, for mistakes if any, he had unknowingly committed while explaining Bhagwan’s infinite glory. This hymn consists of thousand and thirty four slokas describing HIS various incarnations on earth as explained in Vedas. The poetic collection speaks about the glory of Sriman Narayana and sung by Narayana Bhattathiri and for these two reasons, it was named Narayaneeyam. Bhattathiri prayed to Bhagwan to bestow long life, health and prosperity to all those who chant or hear this epic.  

Bhagwan Guruvayoorappan nodded HIS head and immediately granted his request.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ajñātvā te mahattvaṃ yadiha nigaditaṃ viśvanātha kṣamethāḥ
stotraṃ caitat sahasrottaramadhikataraṃ tvatprasādāya bhūyāt |
dvedhā nārāyaṇīyaṃ śrutiṣu ca januṣā stutyatāvarṇanena
sphītaṃ līlāvatārairidam iha kurutāmāyurārogyasaukhyam || 100-11 ||
